articles.content: According to a study by the IW Köln, university housing can only accommodate about 10 % of students, while rents for student apartments rose 2.3 % last year, with Leipzig, Freiburg and Konstanz seeing over 6 % annual increases. In Munich a 30‑m² student flat costs around €840 warm rent, compared with €270 for a WG‑room in Chemnitz, showing stark regional price differences. Researchers warn that despite high demand, new construction is declining because of rising costs, lengthy approval processes and stricter building standards.
articles.title: The battle for the shared apartment room.

articles.content: Researchers use phage‑display technology, which earned the 2018 Chemistry Nobel, to generate antibodies for diagnostic tests without relying on live animals. The method employs a lab‑created library of about ten billion antibody fragments in a one‑millilitre vessel, allowing scientists to select the right antibody and produce it biotechnologically, though the company notes that animal‑derived materials remain essential for patient health.
articles.title: Medical tests without animal suffering.

articles.content: Three teams have been nominated for the German Future Prize, which awards €250,000 for innovative technical developments, and presented their projects at the Deutsches Museum in Munich. One of the projects, from the Hamburg‑based company Traceless Materials, is a biodegradable plastic substitute that breaks down naturally, addressing the environmental problem of long‑chain polymers that do not decompose.
articles.title: Replacement for dentures, laser eye surgery, or hydrogen propulsion?
